{{short description|American mathematician}}
{{use mdy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=June 2020}}
'''Nagambal D.''' "'''Swarna'''" '''Shah''' is an American mathematician and statistician known for her mentorship of students at [[Spelman College]]. She is the founder of the annual StatFest of the [[American Statistical Association]], a leader of the association's Diversity Mentoring Program,{{r|dmp}} and the former chair of the association's Committee on Minorities in Statistics.{{r|mathalliance}}

==Education and career==
Shah is originally from India, where she did her undergraduate studies in mathematics and earned a master's degree in statistics.{{r|mathalliance}} She completed a Ph.D. in statistics in 1970 at the [[University of Windsor]] in Canada.{{r|windsor}}

She joined the Spelman College mathematics department in 1972,{{r|spelman}} and retired to become a professor emerita in 2014.{{r|retire}}

==Recognition==
In 2001, the [[Rollins School of Public Health]] of [[Emory University]] gave Shah their Martin Luther King Jr. Community Service Award.{{r|mlk}} Shah was named a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2010.{{r|dmp}}
The [[National Association of Mathematicians]] gave her their Lifetime Achievement Award in 2017.{{r|nam}}.
The [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] gave her their Lifetime Mentor Award in 2023.{{r|nam}}.
